pool.text: Santo Domingo was founded by the Spanish Empire as an early European settlement.
A major hurricane destroyed Santo Domingo, leading to its rebuilding nearby.
Enslaved Africans led the first major slave revolt on a plantation.
Sir Francis Drake captured the city of Santo Domingo for ransom.
Local militias successfully repulsed an attacking English force sent by Oliver Cromwell.
Criollo bourgeois overthrew the Spanish crown to form a new nation.
Juan Pablo Duarte led the city to gain independence from Haiti.
Hurricane San Zenón struck Santo Domingo, causing severe damage and casualties.
Dictator Rafael Trujillo renamed the capital city to Ciudad Trujillo.
Following an assassination, the city returned to its original name.
Juan Bosch was elected to the presidency in the nation.
The Zona Colonial district became recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
El Quinto Centenario marked the 500th anniversary of Columbus's discovery.
The city hosted the FIBA Americas Championship at a local sports palace.
The local stadium underwent renovation to expand seating and appearance.
Leonel Fernández announced plans to turn the stadium into a modern complex.
The second metro line opened to relieve urban traffic congestion.
A cable car system opened to serve low-income areas and metro lines.
Las Américas handled massive amounts of cargo as a busy airport.
A second cable car line opened to connect a neighboring municipality.
